section_1.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Conditional Probability
section_1.content: Briefly define Conditional Probability P(A|B) using a Venn Diagram animation. Explain it as 'shrinking the universe' to focus only on event B.
section_1.example: Visualizing a drawer of socks: If we know a sock is blue (Event B), what is the probability it is silk (Event A)?

section_2.title: Independence: The 'No Influence' Rule
section_2.content: Define independence as P(A|B) = P(A). Visually demonstrate that knowing B provides zero new information about the occurrence of A.
section_2.example: Flipping a coin (A) and rolling a die (B). The coin doesn't 'care' what the die shows.

section_3.title: The Core of Bayes' Theorem
section_3.content: Introduce Bayes' Theorem as a tool to 'reverse' conditional probability. Use an animation showing the transition from P(Evidence|Hypothesis) to P(Hypothesis|Evidence).
section_3.example: Medical Testing: If a patient tests positive for a rare disease, what is the actual probability they have it? (Prior probability vs. Posterior probability).

section_4.title: Synthesis: Independence vs. Dependency in Bayes
section_4.content: Explain how independence simplifies Bayes' calculation. Show how P(A|B) collapses to P(A) when they are independent, removing the 'diagnostic' power of Bayes.
section_4.example: Predicting a robot's movement: If the sensor reading is independent of the movement, the Bayes calculation effectively ignores the sensor.

section_5.title: Conclusion and Application
section_5.content: Summarize that Bayes is the engine of modern AI (Naive Bayes classifiers). Emphasize that 'Independence' is an assumption that makes computation efficient but sometimes less accurate.
section_5.example: Spam Filters: How your email learns to classify 'Free' (Evidence) as 'Spam' (Hypothesis) using historical probabilities.

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Core of Bayes' Theorem", [
            "Bayes' Theorem reverses conditional probabilities.",
            "We predict the cause from observed evidence.",
            "Start with a prior belief.",
            "Update it using new evidence.",
            "The result is a posterior probability."
        ])
        
        formula = MathTex(r"P(A|B) = \frac{P(B|A) \cdot P(A)}{P(B)}")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.play(Indicate(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        self.play(Circumscribe(formula[0][8:11])) # P(A) - prior

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(CYAN))
        self.play(formula[0][3:8].animate.set_color("#00FFFF")) # P(B|A) - likelihood

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#39FF14"))
        self.play(formula[0][0:5].animate.set_color("#39FF14")) # P(A|B) - posterior
        self.play(Flash(formula))

        self.play(self.lecture_mobjects[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        independent_group = dependent_group.copy()
        independent_group.set_color(BLUE)
        influence_arrow.set_color(BLUE)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(dependent_group.copy(), independent_group),
            FadeOut(influence_arrow),
            ReplacementTransform(dependent_text, independent_text)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture_mobjects[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        reduction_tex = MathTex("P(A|B) = P(A)", color=BLUE)
        self.place_at_grid(reduction_tex, "E3", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(reduction_tex))
        self.wait(2)
